extraction.summary: Aurich and Lustig study the compact orientable flat E6 Hantzsche-Wendt quotient with three half-turn corkscrew holonomies. For the regular case Lx=Ly=Lz, their observer-dependent discrete eigenmodes generate simulated temperature skies. A 51^3 observer grid and simulations over L show that the full-sky scalar S(60°) distribution can be lower than the fixed simply connected ΛCDM comparison near L≈3 LH, while generic observers at L>3 lack the large back-to-back matched circles that their historical search threshold would readily reveal. The kq75 9-year masked simulations retain an enhanced low-S tail for selected L and observer positions. These are conditional simulated signatures, not a topology detection or a fit of the Hantzsche-Wendt model to the observed sky. The authors explicitly restrict the analysis to the direction-averaged C(θ), which discards topology-specific statistical anisotropy.

ideas.title: E6 Hantzsche-Wendt holonomies and the observer-centred Dirichlet cell
ideas.description: The paper defines E3/Γ by three fixed-point-free half-turn corkscrew transformations with scale parameters Lx, Ly, Lz. Squaring a generator gives a pure translation at twice its corresponding scale. The primitive face identifications therefore rotate by π; the topology is inhomogeneous, so the Dirichlet cell and CMB statistics depend on observer position. Dimensionless coordinates x,y,z map to physical coordinates (xLx,yLy,zLz). The detailed CMB results later restrict to Lx=Ly=Lz=L.
locators: Sec. 2 observer-coordinate and Dirichlet-cell discussion, PDF pp.3–5

equations.conventions: Tilded coordinates are Euclidean-cover coordinates; Lx, Ly, Lz are physical topological lengths. The three transformations are transcribed in the displayed order.
equations.domain: The quotient E3/Γ; lengths are positive. The plotted and simulated CMB results use the regular subcase Lx=Ly=Lz.
equations.confidence: high; compared the original HTML MathML/TeX and PDF rendering

ideas.title: Discrete E6 eigenmodes projected about an arbitrary observer
ideas.description: Invariance under Γ yields four related plane waves per eigenmode and a wave-number lattice k⃗=π(nx/Lx,ny/Ly,nz/Lz), with additional allowed-index restrictions stated in the prose. The mode normalization is γ=1/√2 when two indices vanish and γ=1 otherwise. The rotations relate the four wavevectors by π rotations about coordinate axes; their phases are fixed by the integer indices. Re-expansion about observer position x⃗o gives position-dependent α, β and ξlm coefficients. The authors choose Gaussian mode coefficients c=(cR+icI)/√2 with independent zero-mean, unit-variance real and imaginary parts; if any wave-number component vanishes they apply an additional 1/√2 to c because the mode is already real or purely imaginary.
locators: Sec. 2, dimensionless observer coordinates, PDF p.3

equations.expression: Ψk(x⃗)=γ Σ(j=1..4) exp(i k⃗j·x⃗) exp(i φj)
equations.conventions: Four plane-wave terms form one Γ-invariant eigenmode; k⃗j and φj are specified immediately after Eq. (3).
equations.confidence: high; visually checked PDF and inspected HTML math

equations.conventions: The prose restricts the lattice representatives: all-positive or all-negative nonzero triples; one zero component with the other two positive and cyclic permutations; or two zero components with the remaining index even and cyclic permutations. γ=1/√2 for the latter two-zero-component case, otherwise 1.
equations.domain: The discrete spectrum of the quotient, not an unrestricted cubic lattice; k=|k⃗|.

ideas.title: Restricted back-to-back circle searches leave an E6 signature window
ideas.description: The authors argue that the half-turn identifications make the largest circles non-back-to-back. Applying a generator twice gives pure translations but at twice the primitive length and hence smaller back-to-back circles. On a 51^3 observer grid for regular spaces, L>3 has no back-to-back circle with radius >25° for at least some positions and at most one for a position; circles >25° persist only at selected axis-related observers up to roughly L≈6. For L>4.4 the largest non-back-to-back circle can approach zero for some grid observers. The antipodicity angle varies with position. These results identify a blind spot specifically for antipodal searches; they do not show absence of non-back-to-back circles or establish that a real search would detect or exclude them.
locators: Sec. 2, discussion of squared generators and Nα, PDF pp.6–7

ideas.title: Conditional full-sky suppression of the scalar S(60°) statistic
ideas.description: For regular L, the authors compute temperature multipoles from the discrete eigenmodes, then the all-directions-averaged full-sky C(θ) and S(60°). The input transfer function uses their fixed WMAP+BAO+H0 parameter set and full Boltzmann physics; P(k)∝k^(ns−4), with its normalization fitted over l=50–400 to a WMAP seven-year power spectrum. They scan L=1.5–6.0 by 0.1 and L=6–9 by 0.5. At each L, 51^3 observer positions use 50,000 simulations each for position-dependent medians. The reported median is about a factor of two lower than the simply connected comparison for L below about 4; the minimum remains strongly suppressed toward L≈5, while the mean nearly returns to the comparison by L=9. Fig. 9 uses 100,000 simulations for selected positions. Threshold probabilities use 100,000 skies and choose the position with the smallest median. These are conditional simulated distributions and selected-position tail fractions, not fitted probabilities for the observed universe.
locators: Sec. 5.1, Eq. (20) and simulation design, PDF pp.12–16

equations.conventions: k sums over the allowed E6 modes; T_l is the transfer function; ξ includes Gaussian mode amplitudes and observer phases; P(k)∝k^(ns−4).
equations.domain: Temperature multipoles for the paper's fixed flat ΛCDM transfer-function inputs and E6 spectrum.
equations.confidence: high; visually checked PDF and inspected HTML math

ideas.title: WMAP kq75 9-year mask applied to simulated topology skies
ideas.description: The masked-sky pipeline randomly rotates each statistically anisotropic simulated map using uniformly selected Euler angles, removes monopole and dipole, applies the WMAP kq75 9-year mask, computes pseudo-C_l, divides the pseudo-correlation by the mask normalization A(θ), and then computes S(60°). For L=2.7, 3.1, and 4.5 at two selected observers, the paper overlays histograms from 200 cell orientations, with 100,000 simulations per orientation as described. Table 1 reports threshold fractions for those cases, L=9 at one observer, a volume-matched torus case, and ΛCDM with/without the mask. The authors find enhanced low-S fractions relative to the ΛCDM masked simulations. They do not compare a topology-aware likelihood to the observed WMAP map; the mask and WMAP angular spectrum condition a simulation exercise.
locators: Table 1, PDF p.18; Figs. 11–12, PDF pp.19–20; visually checked

equations.domain: Pseudo-correlation estimator for the masked simulated maps; numerical l_max is not stated.

ideas.title: The direction-averaged correlation is insufficient to test topology-specific anisotropy
ideas.description: The authors explicitly note that E6 is statistically anisotropic and that averaging over all direction pairs into C(θ) loses information relative to the covariance C_ll′mm′=⟨a_lm a*_{l′m′}⟩. They state consistency with this isotropic statistic is insufficient because anisotropy tests could conflict with observations; computational cost leads them to restrict the paper to C(θ).
locators: Sec. 4, discussion following Eq. (19), PDF p.11

caveats: The results concern flat Euclidean E6 and, for the principal CMB scan, the regular equal-length branch. They do not test unequal Lx,Ly,Lz or other topologies.

The paper's 2014 back-to-back-circle detectability discussion is tied to historical search pipelines and a radius threshold. It does not rule out the non-back-to-back circles that the paper itself predicts, and no contemporary search is rerun here.

The 513-position notation is 51^3 in the source. Both geometric circle ranges and CMB summaries are sampled on finite observer grids; no continuous observer marginalization or location prior is reported.

C(θ) averages over directions and loses anisotropic covariance information. The authors explicitly state that topology-specific statistical-isotropy tests could be inconsistent with observations, but defer them for computational cost.

The reported low-S fractions are conditional simulations. Full-sky tail probabilities choose an observer with the smallest median; the masked cases also select special observers and random orientations. No correction for position/orientation selection or look-elsewhere effects is reported.

The kq75 mask is applied to simulated skies, but the paper does not report an observed-map topology likelihood, instrument-noise or beam treatment, foreground model, or joint temperature-polarization test. Photon polarization is included in the transfer physics, but no polarization statistic is analyzed.
The masked estimator defines l_max but gives no numerical value; the finite k-mode cutoff, software version, numerical convergence, and exact reproducible implementation are also not stated.

The source says Planck collaboration parameters would not change the largest-scale topological results, but the paper's concrete input set and simulations are WMAP+BAO+H0 conditioned; it reports no Planck map or mask analysis.

Its statements on low CMB correlations and absent convincing matched circles are literature/data context as of 2014. This paper alone cannot establish what changed after 2014 or current detection status.

usefulness.assessment: Useful source for the exact E6 holonomies, observer-dependent discrete mode construction, length and Hubble-unit conventions, and the distinction between antipodal-circle searches and low-C scalar-correlation simulations. It motivates a bounded topology-aware investigation near L≈3 L_H but supplies no accepted cosmological fit, observed-sky detection, or scientific qualification.
usefulness.strongest_objection: The headline compatibility combines two weak summaries while leaving the model's distinctive anisotropy untested: the paper averages away directional covariance for an inhomogeneous topology and compares selected simulation tails rather than a topology-aware likelihood for the actual CMB maps. The selected observer positions and orientations also lack an explicit prior or selection correction. Thus reduced S(60°) plus failure of a restricted antipodal search is feasibility motivation, not evidence that E6 explains the sky.
usefulness.minimal_informative_test: At a predeclared regular scale near L=3 L_H, reproduce the stated discrete spectrum and kq75 pseudo-C_l pipeline with explicit k and l cutoffs and convergence checks. Predeclare observer and cell-orientation distributions instead of selecting the best positions; compare WMAP-era observed cut-sky temperature summaries and topology-specific anisotropic covariance to ΛCDM under the same mask, beam/noise, and foreground treatment. Correct the comparison for scanning L/observer/orientation. A low-S tail alone would remain a conditional statistic, not detection.
